newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian-Dutch Fortis repeats sees 1997 earnings up.
newsitem.headline: Belgian-Dutch Fortis repeats sees 1997 earnings up.

text.p: Belgian-Dutch banking and insurance group Fortis reiterated in its annual report to shareholders that it expects higher earnings in 1997, thanks mainly to its banking operations.

"The organic development of the Fortis companies and the immediate positive contribution of MeesPierson to the profit of Fortis are expected to produce ongoing profit growth in 1997," Fortis, which is co-owned by Belgian Fortis AG and Dutch Fortis AMEV said. "On the basis of this forecast from Fortis, in 1997 both parent companies again expect an increase of earnings per share."
Fortis net profit rose 15.8 percent to 731 million Ecus in 1996. Earnings at Fortis AMEV rose 14.8 percent to 4.42 guilders a share. Those at Fortis AG rose 14.5 percent to 355 francs a share.

In the Netherlands, Fortis said it expected earnings from life insurance activities to increase but non-life earnings to be below "the very good result of 1996". Banking earnings should rise, due to the consolidation of MeesPierson, bought from ABN-AMRO last December, and "because we expect operating profits at VSB Bank to continue to rise in 1997".
In Belgium, Fortis said operating results at the AG 1824 and ASLK-CGER insurance companies would be steady.

"These results will be affected positively by further growth in individual life insurance, and by continuing control of costs and claim ratios. On the other hand, sales of group insurance can be expected to stagnate, due to compulsory governmental wage restraints," Fortis said.
Banking results were expected to be "almost the same as in 1996, in spite of low interest rates and increasing pressure on commercial margins."
Elsewhere in the annual report, Fortis reiterated the company was looking for "selective external growth" alongside growth in its existing businesses.
"Our focus is on a limited number of European countries, the United States and South-East Asia," Fortis said.
Belgian newspaper L'Echo on Wednesday linked Fortis to the forthcoming privatisation of French insurance group GAN. A Fortis spokesman declined to comment, in line with company policy.
